title: Enterprise Agentic Deep Research & Autonomous Knowledge Synthesis

spark.summary: Orchestrate 5-to-15-minute multi-hop autonomous research DAGs without context rot, duplicate web crawls, runaway token spend, or hallucinated citations.
spark.keyTakeaway: If model quality drifts from offline training baselines, bind durable Temporal + LangGraph DAGs with a 450 MB Bloom-filter URL deduplicator, map-reduce context compaction over immutable span_id pointers, and NLI entailment gating.
spark.byteSummary:
Enterprise Agentic Deep Research platforms execute recursive, multi-minute investigation graphs that decompose open-ended queries into 30 to 100 search and browser hops. Unlike single-turn RAG, long-horizon research fails if raw HTML is concatenated into the prompt—causing quadratic attention cost, lost-in-the-middle recall collapse, and unverified citations.

The core architecture pairs a Hierarchical Planner-Researcher-Verifier DAG (Temporal durable execution + LangGraph state machines with Continue-As-New at 40-hop boundaries) with an adaptive fetcher that routes 60% of static pages to fast HTTP clients and 40% of SPA pages to Firecracker Playwright microVMs behind a 450 MB counting Bloom filter.

To prevent context rot and hallucination, map-reduce compaction shrinks 375,000 raw scraped tokens down to 18,000 high-density tokens (95.2% reduction) while retaining immutable ScyllaDB span_id pointers. An NLI entailment gate (tau >= 0.82) verifies every synthesized claim against its cited span before streaming via Last-Event-ID SSE, while Redis Lua token/cost ledgers enforce 85% SLM downgrade and 100% hard-cap circuit breakers.

learningJourney.title: 450 MB Counting Bloom Filter & Single-Flight URL Dedup
learningJourney.purpose: Eliminate redundant web fetches across 250M daily URLs with O(1) memory-bounded filtering.

explanation.foundation: Think of **450 MB Counting Bloom Filter & Single-Flight URL Dedup** as the intuition layer for Enterprise Agentic Deep Research & Autonomous Knowledge Synthesis: Eliminate redundant web fetches across 250M daily URLs with O(1) memory-bounded filtering.
explanation.core: When thousands of concurrent agents explore overlapping topics, duplicate URL fetches waste browser compute and trigger origin 429 bans. A distributed counting Bloom filter sized for N=250M URLs/day at p=0.1% false-positive rate requires 3.59 billion bits (~449.3 MiB) with k=10 MurmurHash3 double-hashing functions, paired with Redis single-flight coalescing for concurrent in-flight URLs.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, 450 mb counting bloom filter & single-flight url dedup becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Architect 100K-job deep research with Continue-As-New @ 40 hops, 449.3 MiB MurmurHash3 Bloom dedup, tau >= 0.82 NLI gating, and Redis Lua budget circuit breakers.

codeExample.code:
import hashlib

def bloom_indices(url: str, m_bits: int = 3_594_395_246, k: int = 10) -> list[int]:
    digest = hashlib.blake2b(url.encode("utf-8"), digest_size=16).digest()
    h1 = int.from_bytes(digest[:8], "little")
    h2 = int.from_bytes(digest[8:], "little") | 1
    return [(h1 + i * h2) % m_bits for i in range(k)]

learningJourney.title: Map-Reduce Context Compaction with Immutable span_id Pointers
learningJourney.purpose: Compress 375K raw scraped tokens to 18K Frontier tokens without losing citation provenance.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Map-Reduce Context Compaction with Immutable span_id Pointers** as the intuition layer for Enterprise Agentic Deep Research & Autonomous Knowledge Synthesis: Compress 375K raw scraped tokens to 18K Frontier tokens without losing citation provenance.
explanation.core: Each scraped document is chunked and persisted as immutable text spans in ScyllaDB + S3, keyed by a content-addressed span_id and SHA-256 hash. Map-stage SLMs extract atomic facts tagged with [span_id], and reduce-stage compaction merges overlapping findings—achieving a 95.2% reduction (375K -> 18K tokens) while keeping every claim cryptographically anchored to its source span.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, map-reduce context compaction with immutable span_id pointers becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Architect 100K-job deep research with Continue-As-New @ 40 hops, 449.3 MiB MurmurHash3 Bloom dedup, tau >= 0.82 NLI gating, and Redis Lua budget circuit breakers.

assumptions: Assumes ScyllaDB for span_id metadata and S3 for raw blobs

codeExample.code:
import hashlib

def register_immutable_span(job_id: str, url: str, raw_text: str, start: int, end: int) -> dict:
    snippet = raw_text[start:end]
    sha256 = hashlib.sha256(snippet.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
    return {
        "span_id": f"span_{sha256[:12]}",
        "job_id": job_id,
        "source_url": url,
        "sha256": sha256,
        "char_range": [start, end]
    }

learningJourney.title: NLI Claim-to-Span Entailment Gate (tau >= 0.82)
learningJourney.purpose: Verify every synthesized claim against its cited span before streaming to the user.

explanation.foundation: Think of **NLI Claim-to-Span Entailment Gate (tau >= 0.82)** as the intuition layer for Enterprise Agentic Deep Research & Autonomous Knowledge Synthesis: Verify every synthesized claim against its cited span before streaming to the user.
explanation.core: Before final report emission, a Natural Language Inference (NLI) cross-encoder scores each generated sentence against the exact raw text fetched from its cited span_id. learningJourney.title: Atomic Redis Lua Budget Guardrails & Cosine Loop Breakers
learningJourney.purpose: Prevent runaway token spend and semantic search loops under 100K concurrent jobs.

explanation.foundation: Each research job carries a USD budget cap enforced atomically via Redis Lua scripts on every LLM and browser call.
explanation.core: At 85% budget consumption, the model router downgrades Frontier LLM calls to a high-speed SLM; at 100%, active child DAGs cancel and force final synthesis.
explanation.deepDive: Simultaneously, a cosine similarity > 0.92 check on consecutive sub-queries trips a semantic loop breaker to prune redundant branches.

assumptions: Assumes atomic Redis Lua cost/hop counters
Assumes 85% SLM downgrade and 100% hard cap

codeExample.code:
-- Atomic Redis Lua budget check
local spent = tonumber(redis.call('INCRBYFLOAT', KEYS[1], ARGV[1]))
local cap = tonumber(ARGV[2])
if spent >= cap then
  return 'HARD_CAP_SYNTHESIZE'
elseif spent >= (cap * 0.85) then
  return 'DOWNGRADE_TO_SLM'
end
return 'ALLOW_FRONTIER'

knowledgeChecks.question: Why does a Temporal-backed deep research orchestrator call Continue-As-New every 40 hops instead of keeping a single workflow execution open for 100+ hops?

options.text: To clear the Redis Bloom filter so previously visited URLs can be re-crawled
options.feedback: The Bloom filter deduplicates URLs across jobs/days; resetting it mid-job would re-introduce duplicate fetches.

options.text: To compact Temporal's append-only event history and prevent hitting history size limits while preserving a clean state snapshot
options.feedback: Correct. Temporal replays event history on worker recovery; Continue-As-New checkpoints a compact snapshot and starts a fresh event log every 40 hops.

options.text: To bypass the NLI entailment threshold on long-running research branches
options.feedback: NLI verification runs independently on synthesized claims and is never bypassed by workflow compaction.

options.text: To upgrade all SLM workers to Frontier LLMs automatically
options.feedback: Model tiering is governed by the Redis Lua budget ledger (85% downgrade threshold), not Temporal history compaction.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Temporal persists every activity and state transition in an event log. Calling Continue-As-New at 40-hop boundaries prevents event-history bloat and replay latency.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does the platform reduce 375,000 raw scraped tokens down to 18,000 Frontier tokens without losing exact citation provenance?

options.text: By truncating each webpage to its first 720 tokens before passing it to the planner
options.feedback: Naive truncation discards key evidence deep inside documents.

options.text: By storing raw HTML inside Redis Cluster and passing full URLs in every prompt
options.feedback: Raw HTML in prompts causes context rot and Redis DRAM bloat.

options.text: By persisting immutable text spans in ScyllaDB/S3 keyed by span_id and passing only span_id pointers through SLM map-reduce compaction
options.feedback: Correct. Immutable span_id pointers let map-reduce compress text by 95.2% while keeping every claim cryptographically anchored to its source span.

options.text: By disabling JavaScript rendering on all Playwright Firecracker microVMs
options.feedback: Disabling JS breaks SPA extraction and does not address token compaction or provenance.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Content-addressed span_id pointers in ScyllaDB + S3 decouple storage of raw evidence from the compacted 18K-token reasoning window.

knowledgeChecks.question: What happens when a deep research job reaches 85% of its USD budget cap in the Redis Lua ledger?

options.text: The job immediately fails with HTTP 402 Payment Required and discards partial results
options.feedback: Discarding 85% of completed research destroys user value; hard cutoff only triggers forced synthesis at 100%.

options.text: The Bloom filter false-positive rate is raised from 0.1% to 10%
options.feedback: Bloom filter sizing is fixed at allocation time and does not control LLM token pricing.

options.text: Temporal deletes the PostgreSQL workflow history to save storage cost
options.feedback: Deleting durable state would break crash recovery.

options.text: The model router dynamically downgrades remaining reasoning hops from Frontier LLMs to a high-speed SLM while reserving budget for final synthesis
options.feedback: Correct. At 85% spend, atomic Redis Lua accounting triggers an SLM downgrade so the job can finish within budget before the 100% hard cap.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Two-tier budget guardrails (85% SLM downgrade, 100% hard cap + forced synthesis) ensure predictable cost bounds without losing completed research.

beginner.summary: Learn how deep research agents break big questions into smaller sub-tasks, avoid visiting the same webpage twice, and verify every fact before writing a report.
beginner.keyTakeaway: If model quality drifts from offline training baselines, bind durable Temporal + LangGraph DAGs with a 450 MB Bloom-filter URL deduplicator, map-reduce context compaction over immutable span_id pointers, and NLI entailment gating.
beginner.byteSummary:
When an AI agent researches a complex topic, it cannot simply dump dozens of entire webpages into one prompt—the model runs out of memory and starts mixing up facts.

Instead, an enterprise deep research system uses a Planner to split the question into smaller sub-goals, checks a fast Bloom filter to avoid fetching duplicate URLs, and uses lightweight HTTP fetchers for simple pages while reserving isolated browsers for JavaScript-heavy sites.

Each source is saved with a unique span_id so summaries never lose their citations, and a final fact-checker verifies that every claim matches its source before streaming the answer.

intermediate.summary: Combine Temporal + LangGraph durable DAGs, a 450 MB Bloom filter, 60/40 adaptive HTTP-to-Firecracker fetching, and map-reduce span_id compaction.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: If model quality drifts from offline training baselines, bind durable Temporal + LangGraph DAGs with a 450 MB Bloom-filter URL deduplicator, map-reduce context compaction over immutable span_id pointers, and NLI entailment gating.
intermediate.byteSummary:
At scale, multi-hop research workflows run for 5 to 15 minutes across 30 to 100 hops. Wrapping LangGraph inside Temporal with Continue-As-New every 40 hops guarantees crash recovery without unbounded event logs.

A 450 MB counting Bloom filter (250M URLs/day, 0.1% FP) paired with Redis single-flight locks prevents duplicate crawls. An adaptive router handles 60% of static pages via async HTTP and escalates 40% to Firecracker Playwright microVMs.

Map-reduce SLM compaction reduces 375K raw tokens by 95.2% to 18K Frontier tokens while preserving ScyllaDB span_id pointers for NLI verification.

advanced.summary: Architect 100K-job deep research with Continue-As-New @ 40 hops, 449.3 MiB MurmurHash3 Bloom dedup, tau >= 0.82 NLI gating, and Redis Lua budget circuit breakers.
advanced.keyTakeaway: If model quality drifts from offline training baselines, bind durable Temporal + LangGraph DAGs with a 450 MB Bloom-filter URL deduplicator, map-reduce context compaction over immutable span_id pointers, and NLI entailment gating.
advanced.byteSummary:
Sustaining 8,333 hops/s across 100K concurrent jobs requires strict physical bounds: 10,000 concurrent Playwright tabs consume ~5.25 TB RAM across 125 bare-metal Firecracker KVM hosts (432 MB/tab).

Every scraped span is content-addressed by SHA-256 into ScyllaDB + S3, enabling 95.2% map-reduce compaction without citation detachment. An NLI cross-encoder enforces tau >= 0.82 entailment on all claims prior to Last-Event-ID SSE streaming.

Atomic Redis Lua ledgers enforce 85% Frontier-to-SLM downgrade and 100% hard-cap synthesis, while cosine > 0.92 loop breakers prune cyclic exploration.
